title: Russia violates Polish airspace as missiles and drone crash near NATO exercise, Warsaw calls it a provocation
summary: Poland said two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone violated its airspace overnight during a massive attack on Ukraine, landing near a Coalition of the Willing exercise. Warsaw called it an intentional provocation and said it would seek additional NATO forces. No casualties were reported.
content:
Poland said on Friday that Russia had violated its airspace three times overnight, in what Warsaw denounced as a deliberate provocation, after two Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone came down on Polish territory during a massive Russian attack on Ukraine.

Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz told a news conference that the three objects fell in southeastern Poland: a Kh-101 cruise missile in the village of Nowy Lipowiec, a second missile in the town of Rudnik nad Sanem, and a jet-powered drone in the village of Molodycz. "There has been a violation of Polish airspace and an incursion by objects from the Russian Federation," he said, according to [Al Jazeera's report from Warsaw](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/20/poland-condemns-russian-provocation-after-airspace-violations).

Polish authorities said there were no casualties and no damage to critical infrastructure inside Poland. Emergency services and military personnel secured the three sites, and prosecutors opened investigations into the possible airspace violations. An object about seven metres long fell near Nowy Lipowiec at around 0540 GMT, according to local officials, and security camera footage from a nearby property showed an explosion in the distance.

The incursions came during one of the largest Russian assaults on Ukraine of the entire war. Russian forces attacked Ukraine overnight and into the morning with roughly 100 ballistic and cruise missiles alongside 404 drones, according to Ukrainian officials cited by The New Voice of Ukraine. The strikes killed eight people in Kyiv and injured 28 across nine regions, according to the city's mayor, Vitali Klitschko, and Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky, and knocked out electricity, water and heating supplies in parts of the capital and beyond.

Poland's Armed Forces Operational Command said its air defence systems were activated at around 3:30 a.m. local time as the Russian attack unfolded. Polish and allied aircraft remained airborne through the night, and the government issued alerts for 20 districts across the Lublin and Podkarpackie regions that border Ukraine. Operational Commander Gen. Ireneusz Nowak said Polish air defence had tracked 11 aerial objects operating near the border overnight, three of which violated Polish airspace.

What makes this incident especially serious is where the weapons fell. Nowy Lipowiec lies about 60 kilometres from the Ukrainian border and roughly 76 kilometres from Nowa Deba, where troops from Britain and other European allies are conducting "Exercise Koalicja", a Coalition of the Willing drill running from November 9 to 22 to prepare for a possible post-war mission in Ukraine. The exercise is designed to help stabilise Ukraine and rebuild its military once the war ends, and the missile landed less than a two-hour drive from the training ground.

Kosiniak-Kamysz said Warsaw's allies shared its assessment that the incursion was no accident. "We know that what landed on Polish soil came from Russia. Therefore, and this is not just my own assessment, but also that of our foreign partners, including those within NATO, it does not look like an accident," he said. "It appears that we are dealing with an intentional provocation." Prime Minister Donald Tusk convened an emergency meeting with ministers, military officials and security service chiefs, and Poland said it would request additional NATO forces, according to The New Voice of Ukraine. Britain's prime minister condemned the violation, Reuters reported.

The incident is the most serious breach of Polish airspace since September, when NATO jets shot down Russian drones that had entered Poland during another large attack on Ukraine, prompting Warsaw to invoke NATO's Article 4 consultations. That episode established a precedent: an airspace violation by Russia now triggers immediate allied consultations and a visible reinforcement of NATO's eastern flank, and Friday's events are likely to follow the same path.

Analysts cited by The Telegraph suggested Moscow may have had a dual objective: testing Polish air defences and NATO's response time, while sending a direct warning to Poland and other European countries that supporting Ukraine carries consequences. Investigators have not yet established whether the objects entered Polish territory deliberately or as a consequence of their flight paths during the attack on Ukraine, and that distinction matters for how NATO responds.

The timing adds a further layer of tension. The incursion came a day after the leaders of the United States, China and Russia met in Shenzhen and issued a joint declaration, and as American envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff press ahead with closed-door peace talks. President Donald Trump told European leaders this week that President Vladimir Putin "wants to end the war, he wants the deal done," according to sources cited by Axios, and [Kushner has discussed NATO membership for Ukraine in the talks](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/trump-tells-kushner-putin-tired-of-war-ready-settlement-november-2026). Friday's missile landings in Poland are a reminder of how far apart the battlefield and the negotiating table remain.

For now, the immediate questions are practical ones: what exactly fell where, whether any of the wreckage poses a danger, and what reinforcements NATO will send. The longer question is political. Russia's war has now spilled onto the territory of a NATO member for the second time in just over two months, and each incident narrows the space between an accident that can be managed and a provocation that demands an answer. Poland has made clear which side of that line it believes Friday's events fall on, and its allies will have to decide whether they agree. The [collapse of talks on a Black Sea energy truce earlier this month](https://new-sfeed.lovable.app/en/articles/putin-rules-out-black-sea-energy-truce-crimea-bridge-november-2026) showed how quickly de-escalation efforts can unravel, and Friday's events suggest the coming days will test NATO's unity as much as its defences.
